subjective.citation_text: Patient: I'm 60 years old, male, and I'm here because I've been having numbness and tingling in both of my hands for a few weeks now. It started after my car wreck last December when I broke both wrists, and it's gotten worse over the last month. Doctor: Can you describe the progression of the numbness and tingling in your hands? Have you noticed any associated pain, and does the sensation radiate to your arms or fingers? Additionally, have you undergone any prior treatments or interventions for your wrist fractures or neurological symptoms? Patient: The numbness and tingling started after my car wreck last December when I broke both wrists. At first, it wasn’t too bad, but once the fractures healed, it got worse, especially over the last month. It’s mainly in my hands, but sometimes it feels like it goes up my arms. I’ve been wearing splints on both wrists, though the right one is worse. I was given some nerve pain medicine, but I haven’t been taking it like I should. Doctor: Have you undergone any neurological evaluations or imaging studies, such as an MRI or EMG, to assess the extent of nerve involvement following your wrist fractures? Patient: No, I haven't had any neurological evaluations or imaging studies like an MRI or EMG yet. The doctor mentioned scheduling me for a nerve test, though, to figure out exactly what's going on. Doctor: Could you please confirm if you have been scheduled for the nerve test, and if so, when is it planned? Additionally, have you experienced any changes in hand strength or difficulty performing daily tasks due to the numbness and tingling? Patient: I haven't had the nerve test yet, but the doctor said I need to schedule it. As for my hands, they do feel weaker, especially when I'm using them, and it's been harder to grip things or do things like button my shirt or turn doorknobs without the tingling messing with me. Doctor: Has the patient experienced any weakness or difficulty with fine motor tasks in the hands
